chunks: The position of the one who holds authority is like the thread of the beads, which gathers and unites them.
If the thread is broken, they disperse and are lost, and never come together again in their entirety.
The Arabs today, even though few in number, are many because of Islam, and strong because of unity.
So be their axis, and rotate the mill with the Arabs, and be their root; avoid the fire of war.
For if you leave this land, the Arabs will attack you from its edges and corners, until the weak points you leave behind become more important to you than those before you.

key_terms.الْقَيِّمِ بِالأَمْرِ: The one who holds authority / head of government

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used by Imam Ali to explain the importance of the leader's presence in maintaining political unity?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of the 'thread of the beads' to illustrate that the Caliph’s physical presence is the central axis (Qutb) holding the Arab tribes together; without it, the unity fractures irreversibly. He advises Umar to remain in the land to manage internal tribal dynamics, warning that his departure would trigger a multi-front crisis where internal vulnerabilities would outweigh external military gains.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The position of the head of government is that of the thread for beads, as it connects them and keeps them together.
If the thread is broken, they will disperse and be lost, and will never come together again.
The Arabs today, even though small in number are big because of Islam and strong because of unity.
You should remain like the axis for them, and rotate the mill (of government) with (the help of) the Arabs, and be their root. Avoid battle,
because if you leave this place the Arabs will attack you from all sides and directions till the unguarded places left behind by you will become more important than those before you.
